changesets.headline: A swizzled component and the package's components now announce through one pair of live regions: messages from both join the same frame, and a copy no longer mounts a second pair that screen readers would read twice or skip. The modal announcement route is shared the same way. No API changes.

BottomSheet: a finger's pull on the sheet's content at a scroll edge cancels the content's native pan as soon as the pull reaches a tap's wobble (5 px), before the sheet's own drag begins at 8 px. In iOS Safari the first `touchmove` a page keeps committed the touch to the content's scroll, so a slow-starting swipe down rubber-banded the content under the finger while the sheet moved beside it. A tap that wobbles less than 5 px keeps its click, while a tap that wobbles 5 to 8 px toward the edge now loses it. A real scroll is never cancelled. A mostly sideways swipe on a horizontal row is not cancelled before the sheet's drag begins; a first move past 8 px starts the drag in any direction, as before.
`astryx discover` lists the experimental TabBarMoreList component from `@astryxdesign/lab`.
Add hook documentation and interactive sparkline example block for `useDirection`, detailing render-time direction handling and CSS logical properties best practices.

InternationalizationProvider has a calendar example: the provider's `calendar` prop shows a `Calendar` and a `DateInput` in the Japanese or Buddhist calendar, and the value stays a Gregorian ISO date. Both calendars work without `Temporal`.

Icon sets: a project picks one main icon set and backup sets in order, and an icon no set has becomes a placeholder in the copied file. Only the experimental icon commands, projects that set `experimental.iconSet`, templates that declare `icons`, and the icon-set guide change.
changesets.body:
- **Main set and backups.** `astryx experimental icon use <main> --backup <set>` (repeatable, order kept) writes `experimental.iconSet` as a list, the main set first; with no `--backup` it writes the plain string as before. The receipt adds `backups`, the installed sets the list leaves out (`unlisted`), and the command that adds them (`next`). `experimental icon --list` shows the `order` and each set's `role` and `rank`, and, when two or more sets are installed and none is the main set, the command to run. A CLI before 0.7.12 refuses the list form, and `use` warns when the project's CLI range admits one.
- **Copied templates follow the list.** `astryx template` takes each icon from the first set in the list that has its meaning, never mixing sets within one icon, and reports the set used, a missing look (`variant: {asked, used}`), and each set used with its license (`icons.sets`).
- **No stray library imports.** An icon no set in the list loses the template's original import. The copied file declares a small `MissingIcon` component once (a dashed square, 1em, in the current text color, hidden from screen readers unless a use gives it a label), and each place the icon was renders it, with a comment naming the meaning. It needs no new package. The output prints a note naming the meaning and both fixes (map it in the main set, or add a backup set), and the JSON lists it in `icons.placeholder`.
- **Doctor.** With the opt-in, the `icon-sets` check fails when the list names a set that is not installed, withdrawn, or shipped by two packages, and when more than one set is installed and the list leaves one out. A new `icon-placeholders` check warns while copied code still uses the placeholder, naming each file and meaning; a commented-out or quoted copy does not count. Projects that have not opted in see no change.
- **Labeled template icons.** Every icon a bundled template uses now declares its meaning, with 30 new icon definitions. `integration check` notes an icon a template imports but does not declare (`template_icon_undeclared`), in a package whose templates declare `icons`: an import from a module the package declares icons from, which the template renders as an element with no children or passes as a value. Any other import from that module, such as a type, a function it calls, or a provider with children, is listed as not checked. The note fails `--strict --next` and leaves `--strict` as it was. A generic renderer (a bare `Icon`, or one every use gives an icon prop) and an import that matches an icon by its name only are listed as not checked instead.

changesets.headline: A swizzled overlay that carries its own copy of the layer runtime now shares the package's: one layer stack, one modal outlet order, one gesture counter, and one record of outside dismissals, popover show and hide operations, layer surfaces and press claims per page. Before, such a copy kept its own, so Escape over a swizzled HoverCard inside a package Dialog could close the Dialog too, and the two copies could race each other's popover operations or miss each other's outside presses. No API changes.

A disabled Link stays announced as disabled, with its own role, when the caller also passes `aria-disabled` or `role`. Before, those caller props replaced Link's own, so `aria-disabled={false}` announced a disabled link as enabled, and `role="button"` announced a button that does nothing.
Markdown's public parser drops every data: link and image URL, and `<Markdown>` renders data: links and images as source text.

dependency floors move to current releases: the build package needs autoprefixer 10.6.2, browserslist 4.29.5 and lightningcss 1.33.0; the CLI needs ignore 7.0.14, jscodeshift 17.4.0, linkedom 0.18.15, zod 4.6.7 and @stylexjs/babel-plugin 0.19.1; each theme needs lucide-react 1.66.0. Peer ranges do not change.

Internal: Table's row virtualization now runs on one shared list-windowing module inside Core, which later long lists will reuse. The undocumented `@astryxdesign/core/internal/virtualization` entry gives Lab the same module. Table's behavior and public API do not change. Internal entries are outside the public API and its compatibility promise.
Carousel snap paging: in Safari, a held row's stops and span stay on each item's start edge when the settle moves between an item's rect read and its translate read.

Tokenizer forwards BaseTypeahead's `menu` and `onOpenChange` in its inline presentation, and its handle gains `open()` and `close()`. A token whose own button calls `open()` with a dialog-role menu opens the dialog, and Escape returns focus to that token: focus that a press puts on a token's control, and the menu's focus return, stay there instead of moving to the input. The sheet presentation keeps its own sheet.
The CLI adds a `BaseTypeaheadMenu` block: a BaseTypeahead whose listbox menu shows information around the result list, and whose pick or filter button opens a dialog-role menu on the same layer.

Typeahead: Backspace or Delete on the selected Token clears the value, as the clear button does, when the clear button shows: it calls `onChange(null)`, announces the cleared value, and moves focus to the empty input. Without `hasClear`, the keys start editing, as a click does.
